observations: Torah 93 is one of the briefest entries in Likutay Moharan Tinyana — it is not a formal Torah but a single reported statement ('שָׁמַעְתִּי בִּשְׁמוֹ'). It contains no thematic elaboration, no layered conceptual identification, and no bechina language of the Rebbe's own coinage. The sole concepts mentioned are: תְּפִלָּה (prayer), הִתְבּוֹדְדוּת (personal prayer / hitbodedut), מַחֲלֹקֶת (dispute/opposition), and the Talmudic phrase 'דְּבָרִים הָעוֹמְדִים בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם' (things that stand at the height of the world). The relationship between these concepts is explanatory and causal (eitza): prayer is lofty → people treat it lightly → therefore the Rebbe, whose entire work was prayer, was opposed. There is no cluster of three or more concepts connected through explicit bechina language forming an independent thematic domain. The minimum condition for a new package (three concepts joined by bechina language in an independent domain) is not met. No new packages are proposed.
